The petitioners' case is that they had their ancestral home on 2.65 acres out of a total of 5.80 acres of Khatian No. 1358 of mouzaMoulvi Bazar Town which comprises several houses, tank, graveyard, gardens etc. wherein the petitioners have been living for generations now. The respondent No.4 Syed Mohsin Ali, his six brothers, two sisters and mother mutated their names in respect of the entire land of 5.80 acres of the above khatian No. 1358 on the basis of a registered Kabala No. 5879 executed and registered on 31.10.55 by one Keramat Ali in favour of Syed Ashraf Ali, deceased father of the said respondent No.4. The said Keramat Ali auction purchased the entire land of 5.80 acres of the said khatian No. 1358 on 25.9.54 for arrears of rent. The auction purchaser Keramat Ali however sold only 3.15 acres of the khatian land out of 5.80 acres to late Syed Ashraf Ali, father of the respondent No.4. The balance 2.65 acres of ancestral homestead continued to remain in the possession of the petitioners and their predecessors. The predecessors of the petitioners obtained a registered Muktipatra dated 8.5.79 from one of the sons of auction purchaser Keramat Ali, namely HabiburRahman. Thereafter the predecessors of the petitioners by executing and registering three separate deeds of gift, all dated 5.11.78, transferred their right, title and interest in the case land to the petitioners and delivered physical possession thereof to them. The petitioners thereafter instituted Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979 be- fore the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvibazar. After compliance of necessary formalities all the three mutation cases were allowed vide order dated 13.11.79. The respondent No.4 Syed Mohsin Ali and his 5 brothers filed an objection petition before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar whereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1979 was started. The par- ties were notified. After hearing the parties the Circle Officer forwarded the case record to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet for necessary action with a detailed report as he found the case to be complicated. Then the respondent No.4 preferred an appeal before the Additional Deputy Com- missioner (Revenue), Sylhet under section 147 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, shortly the Act, against the Order dated 13.11.79 passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar whereupon Mutation Appeal Case No. 24 of 1979- 80 was started and the petitioners were notified. By his order dated 10.9.80 the Additional Deputy Com- missioner, Sylhet after hearing the parties rejected the appeal of the respondent No.4 and upheld the or- der dated 13.1l.79 passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvibazar in Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979. Against the aforesaid order of the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet the respondent No.4 preferred an appeal before the Com- missioner, Chittagong Division being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 223 of 1980 under section 147 of the Act which was heard and disposed of by the Additional Commissioner, Chittagong Division by his order dated 15.12.82 dismissing the same and con-firming the order dated 10.9.80 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet. 

 8. It is stated therein that the aforesaid 5.80 acres of land of the aforesaid khatian originally be-longed to Syed Ashraf Ali, the father of respondent No.4, and Syed Ashraf Ali gifted the same to his wife SyedaAktarunnessaKhanam in lieu of her dower. The said property was sold in auction for arrears of rent and was purchased by Keramat Ali when Syed Ashraf Ali and his wife were living in Calcutta. Coming to know of the auction sale Syed Ashraf Ali obtained a kabala in his own name for valuable consideration from the said auction purchaser Keramat Ali in respect of the whole of the auction sold property, namely 5.80 acres, by kabala No. 5879 dated 31.10.55. But unfortunately the deed writer through bonafide mistake wrote 3.15 acres in place of the whole of the auction sold property, namely 5.80 acres. The recipient of the said kabala, Syed Ashraf Ali, was not aware of the said mistake in the deed as he remained in possession of the whole of 5.80 acres all along, including the period from the date of auction upto the date of the aforesaid kabala. 

 9. During the rent roll operations in 1958 the entire 5.80 acres of land was wrongly recorded in the names of Syed Ashraf Ali and his brother Syed Ankar Ali, the latter having no title to or interest in the aforesaid property. In 1964 Syed Ashraf Ali allowed his nephews, namely, Syed Abdul Mannan, Syed Mozammel Ali and Syed SalehMasud to live in a portion of the aforesaid property having structures thereon, as his licencees. In 1965 Syed Ashraf Ali corrected the khatian by filing Case No. 331 of 1965 before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar by striking out of the name of his brother Syed Ankar Ali from the khatian. It is therefore absolutely incorrect that the balance 2.65 acres of ancestral home- stead continued to remain in possessive of the petitioners and their predecessors. Three nephews of Syed Ashraf Ali were only in possession of a part of the property in question. Syed Ashraf Ali died in 1970. Thereafter the heirs of Syed Ashraf Ali, namely, the respondent No.4 and his brothers and sisters requested the said licencees to surrender possession of the structures to them. At this stage they became hostile and instead of complying with the request they approached one of the sons of auction purchaser Keramat Ali, namely HabiburRahman, and obtained a so-called Muktipatrafrom him in respect of 2.65 acres out of the khatian taking advantage of mistake in respect of area in Syed Ashraf Ali's kahala dated 31.10.55 The said Muktipatra dated 8.5.79 was obtained in the names of the three licencees of Syed Ashraf Ali and another, namely Syed Abdun Noor. The Muktipatra is collusive and fraudulent. Later, Syed Abdun Noor purported to gift .64 acres of land in favour of his brother's son, namely petitioner No. 1, on 26.10.79. Syed Abdul Mannan purported to gift .65 acre on the same day to his wife who is the petitioner No. 2. Syed SalehMasud purported to gift .65 acres of land on the same day to his wife, petitioner No.3. The said donors being mere licencees and having no title to the land in question, the petitioners got no title to or interest in the lands purported to have been gifted to them. It has also been stated that after completing the aforesaid collusive and fraudulent transactions the petitioners applied to the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar for mutation of their names whereupon their names were mutated in respect of 1.95 acres by an ex parte order dated 13.11.79. No notice of the aforesaid mutation ease was either issued or served upon the respondent No.4 and the order of mutation was passed in spite of objection raised by the Tahsildar which will appear from the records of the Mutation Case Nos. 91, 92 and 93 of 1979. Thereafter the respondent No.4 has more or less accepted the petitioners' description of the progress of the case from the stage of the Circle Officer (Revenue), Moulvi Bazar upto the Board of Land Administration. The said respondent however justifies his appeal before the Ministry of Land Administration on the ground that the law does not oust the Government's authority to decide a matter in respect of which the Board of Land Administration exercises appellate power. 

 It may be stated that formerly appeal lay to the Government against an order made by the Commissioner of a Division but by the Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. XLI of 1982) in place of the word 'Government' the words 'Board of Land Administration' were substituted.
